Subject: Private deployment - limited audit window & satellite node access

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. AeroMed is excited about moving forward with Redwood Private, but our compliance and operations teams identified two constraints we need to reflect in the contract before procurement can sign:

1) Audit window: for operational impact reasons we can only accommodate on-site or VPN-based audits during a 4-hour, pre-windowed maintenance slot (we call these "satellite windows") — once per quarter. We need Redwood to agree to provide required logs and limited on-prem access within that window only.

2) Satellite node access: we operate a small number of satellite inference nodes in our hospital DMZs. Security requires that Redwood engineers only access these nodes via our jump host during pre-approved windows and under our escort.

We know these are non-standard asks. From a commercial perspective, procurement is asking if Redwood can provide a 10% pilot credit and accept the limited audit schedule and access constraints for the first 12 months. Can you advise if that’s feasible and what approvals you’ll need? We can send the formal SOC and audit checklist if helpful.

Appreciate your help — Emma

-- 
Emma Collins
Head of IT Compliance, AeroMed Health
emma.collins@aeromedhealth.com

Forwarding AeroMed request — they want a carveout for audit windows (4hr quarterly) and constrained jump-host access to satellite nodes. Procurement is asking for a 10% pilot credit and a 12-month acceptance period for these constraints.

My read: security impact is moderate but operationally we can work the access model (jump host + escort + session recordings). The sticky items for Deal Desk / Execs are:
- KMS / key material: they asked us to accept local KMS escrow during the pilot (we should avoid escrow if possible).
- Audit cadence & scope: limiting audits to 4 hours is unusual; it could be OK if we require pre-submitted evidence and remote logs to reduce on-site time.
- Pricing: 10% pilot credit for 12 months for the private deployment (expected ~ $420k ARR) — comp takes a hit, would need exec sign-off for >5% credit.

Attachments: Aeromed_Audit_Request_20260921.pdf (their checklist), Proposed_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (my proposed 3-step runbook), Redwood_Limited_Audit_Playbook_v1.pdf (ops/security mitigation suggestions).

Ask: Can I get an executive authorization for: (1) one-time approval for the 10% pilot credit (or counter if you prefer), (2) acceptance of the limited audit window model for the first 12 months conditioned on providing remote artifacts + session recordings, and (3) temporary, monitored jump-host access under AeroMed escort (no long-term KMS escrow). I can tee up legal language for a rider.

Thanks — Aditya

-- 
Aditya Rao

Aditya — thanks for the summary. A few quick points:

1) Commercial: I'm willing to approve a 10% pilot credit for the first 12 months as a customer success pilot (to secure the account and given the strategic nature of AeroMed). That exceeds Deal Desk standard thresholds, so I need Markus or Kimberly to sign off.

2) Security: we should require a formal playbook (you've attached one) and insist on remote log exports + a short pre-audit checklist that AeroMed must complete 7 days prior. If Security gives a green light on the playbook we can accept the 4-hour slot restriction for the pilot.

3) KMS/escrow: no KMS escrow unless Legal + Security sign off and it is bounded (timeboxed to pilot + indemnity language). We should push for customer-managed keys with HSM integration instead of escrow.

Next step: Kimberly — can you confirm security's comfort with the proposed playbook and the temporary jump-host model? Markus — can you approve the 10% credit for this pilot (DW-2026-1432)? If approved I will instruct Deal Desk to prepare the commercial rider and I’ll loop Legal to draft the timebound language.

-Lauren

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the playbook and the proposed mutual action plan. Security's position: we can accept a 4-hour quarterly on-site window for the pilot only if all of the following are true:

- AeroMed provides a complete pre-audit evidence bundle (logs, configuration snapshots) at least 72 hours beforehand.
- All engineer sessions into the satellite nodes are recorded and retained for 90 days (we'll provide our session capture template).
- No permanent key escrow: customer-managed KMS with HSM + access mediated by a signed temporary token for each session (timeboxed).

If AeroMed accepts those constraints, security will sign off on a 12-month timeboxed pilot with limited audit windows. We will not agree to open-ended escrow.

One technical caveat: we need Deal Desk to confirm the credit band and ensure commercial acceptance includes the security obligations and an SLA carveout for the pilot period.

-Kimberly

1) Approve up to 10% pilot credit for 12 months (DW-2026-1432) provided Legal signs a timeboxed rider that captures the exact audit scope and data access model.
2) No KMS escrow or permanent key custody — customer-managed KMS required; temporary session tokens only.
3) Require the pre-audit evidence bundle 72 hours before any on-site window; session recordings retained for 90 days and accessible to Redwood security on request.

Aditya — please send AeroMed a short note with the conditions above and the next steps. Lauren, please ask Deal Desk + Legal to draft the rider and tag this for expedited review. Kimberly, please hand-off any session-capture templates we need to share.

Markus
